subject: Aligning POC lab: prompt review, tiering, and regional fallback walk-through
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@olisys.com>, Olisys Platform Team <eng@olisys.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Aligning POC lab: prompt review, tiering, and regional fallback walk-through

Hi Jordan / Olisys team,

Thanks again for agreeing to run the hands-on POC with us. To make the workshop productive for both teams, we'd like to split the kickoff into two focused blocks: prompt & routing policy review (where we align on model tiering and fallback rules) and a separate load-test session (to validate throughput and KV/prefix caching).

Options that work for our core team (PST):
- Option A: Wed Jan 14, 10:00–12:00 PST (single longer working session)
- Option B (preferred by product/engineering): Thu Jan 15, 09:00–10:00 PST — prompt + routing policy; Fri Jan 16, 14:00–16:00 PST — load tests and failover validation

Attached: poc_agenda_v1.pdf and prompt_set_v2.csv (short pre-read; please flag any prompts you want us to remove or anonymize). Evelyn will bring the load harness but has a hard constraint on Fri afternoon.

Can you confirm which option is best, and who from your side should join (security, platform, SRE)? Also note any regional attendees so we can avoid timezone friction.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: poc_agenda_v1.pdf, prompt_set_v2.csv
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@olisys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olisys Platform Team <eng@olisys.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 12:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Aligning POC lab: prompt review, tiering, and regional fallback walk-through

Marissa, thanks — this looks great. Quick note: we have a standing exec review on Wed 10–11 PST so Option A won't work for our leads. Option B is promising but I have one ask: can we shift the prompt + routing block to 13:00–14:00 EST (which would be 10:00–11:00 PST) to get our East Coast SREs included?

We will also want our security contact on the routing discussion: Alex Garcia (alex.garcia@olisys.com). Also, if possible, add a brief pre-read on what fallback tiers look like for regional outages — our SREs will want to see the tiering matrix ahead of time.

Happy to take the two-block approach you suggested if we can land times that work for both sides.

— Jordan
Jordan Price | Head of Platform, Olisys
jordan.price@olisys.com

Subject: Re: Aligning POC lab: prompt review, tiering, and regional fallback walk-through

+1 on splitting. To keep momentum, propose two compact, outcome-driven blocks instead of a long session:
- Block 1 (prompt review + routing policy): 60 minutes — align on model selection and fallback tiers, capture concrete canaries and A/B playbook.
- Block 2 (load tests): 90–120 minutes — verify steady-state throughput and graceful degradation scenarios.

If Olisys prefers East Coast overlap, we can do Block 1 on Thu Jan 15 at 13:00–14:00 EST (10:00–11:00 PST). For Block 2, engineering prefers Fri Jan 16 afternoon — we'll confirm exact window with Evelyn. I'll bring a short model shortlist (13B/7B quantized variants) and an initial tiering matrix so we can decide cutovers.

Karthik
Product Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@olisys.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aligning POC lab: prompt review, tiering, and regional fallback walk-through

Engineering constraint: our load harness and test infra are booked Thu AM for another onboarding. The earliest contiguous window we can guarantee the load-test run (including KV-cache warm-up and two failover scenarios) is Fri Jan 16, 14:00–16:00 PST. I attached the test config we'll run so you can scan it for any non-starter limits (load-test-config.yaml).

Notes: the run includes: steady-state at 250 rps equivalent (mixed prompt lengths), a simulated us-east outage where traffic is shifted to us-west, and a short cold-start spike to validate KV cache priming. Please confirm if Olisys needs us to lower peak RPS or alter the regional failover pattern.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — finalizing as follows to accommodate both teams:

1) Thu Jan 15, 2026 — 13:00–14:00 EST / 10:00–11:00 PST — Block 1: Prompt review + routing policy (model shortlist, tiering matrix, fallback rules).
2) Fri Jan 16, 2026 — 14:00–16:00 PST — Block 2: Load-test run + failover validation (Evelyn's harness).

I created calendar invites and linked the invite here: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=olisys-poc-20260114. HubSpot record: HS-24355.

Pre-reads (attached): poc_agenda_v1.pdf, prompt_set_v2.csv, load-test-config.yaml. Jordan — I've added Alex Garcia as requested; please let me know if there are any additional compliance folks to include.

Action items before Block 1:
- Olisys: confirm attendees (SRE, platform, security) and flag any prompts to remove from prompt_set_v2.csv.
- Redwood: finalize model shortlist and publish the tiering matrix (Karthik).

I'll send a short meeting note after Block 1 with decisions and roll-forward items for the load run.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Confirmed on our side — both blocks look good. Alex from security will join the routing block; our SRE lead (sre-lead@olisys.com) will join the load run.

One ask: can Redwood circulate a 2–3 slide pre-read on the fallback tiers (what triggers a tier switch, expected latency delta, AND estimated cost delta) before Thu's session so we can triage quickly? Thanks — Jordan
